alignments.note: Substantival article takes the pronoun the ASV supplies to make the participle a clause subject, under rule 41.
Participle rendered as a finite verb; *out* is the particle of the English phrasal verb *send out*, kept with the verb under rule 44 as `שָׁלַח` → *put forth* is.
Pronominal suffix as possessive under rule 18.
Construct noun keeps only its own word.
Bare directional nominal: the supplied *upon* states what it contributes to the clause and joins its unit under rule 33.
Pronominal suffix as possessive under rule 18.
Construct noun keeps only its own word.

The `עַד` of the adverbial `עַד־מְהֵרָה` takes the degree word the ASV writes for it, the noun keeping *swiftly*. The competing reading marks the preposition `unrepresented` under rule 40 and folds *very* into the noun's unit; I took the division because rule 11 gives a present morpheme the English word its sense carries before a supplied-word analysis, and two English words answer to the two morphemes here.
Noun rendered as the English adverb *swiftly*.
